_about: Who built a dungeon and what for, how it fell, who used it after, why it is still unlooted and what the town makes of it: the history half of a dungeon's concept (rules/dungeons.py, `concept_for`). The owner, 2026-11-16: 'A proper dungeon cannot just be random rooms and it must hold a cohesive story/pattern.' Shaped on Hal Johnson's origin / history / ecology (haljohnsonbooks.substack.com, 'Anatomy of a dungeon', 2024), Sly Flourish's three layers - what it was built for, what it became, what it is now (slyflourish.com/making_awesome_dungeons.html) - and the ruin questions of Kevin Crawford's Worlds Without Number (type, age, how ruined, why unplundered, previous users, what the locals think, one ruin tag). Authored game data: no model writes a word of it. Slots a sentence may carry, filled in code from the world's own names or the generic `who` below: {builders} {users} {town} {where} {age} {leader} {lair} {ally}. A builder's `ground` says which of the world's records may name it: `people` (a PEOPLE entity of the continent), `nation` (a NATION), `faction` (a faction whose own description carries one of `words`); with none of those it is its generic `who`. `rooms` are by family (built: ruins, crypt, sewers, cellar, tower; natural: cave; dug: mine), ordered from the way in to the innermost. `traps` are content/rules/traps.json ids that fit the builders. `traces` are what the builders left that can still be seen, one per room, shown and never explained. `ruin`, where a row has it, limits how the place can have fallen to the causes that make sense for it (nobody walls up a cave its builders never dug).

tomb.purpose: a tomb, to keep their honoured dead

built: the antechamber
a low room with a stone bench along each wall, for the mourners
the hall of offerings
shelves cut into the walls, and the dust of what was left on them
the embalmers' room
a stone table with a channel cut round its edge
natural: the barrow mouth
a cave mouth walled up with dressed stones, half of them pulled down
the bone shelf
a ledge of rock where the bones were laid out to dry
the cairn chamber
a cave chamber with a cairn of river stones heaped in the middle

traces: Names are cut over every niche, worn almost smooth, all of them names of {builders}.
A carved lintel shows a procession carrying a bier down into the dark, and the faces are the faces of {builders}.
Grave-goods are still set out in rows: cups, combs, a child's clay horse, nothing anybody thought worth stealing.

temple.purpose: a shrine below the ground, for rites kept out of the daylight

built: the narthex
a vestibule with a dry basin by the door for washing the hands
the hall of pillars
a long hall, its pillars carved as figures holding up the roof
the vestry
rotted chests where the vestments were kept, the cloth gone to threads
natural: the washing pool
a pool in the rock, its edge cut into steps
the painted gallery
a cave wall covered from floor to roof in faded paint
the echo chamber
a round cave where every sound comes back three times

traces: The painted figures on the walls are {builders} at their rites, kneeling to something the paint has flaked away from.
Prayers are scratched into the floor stones by the hundred, in the hand of {builders}.
An altar stone stands at the end, cracked clean across, and the crack has been filled with lead.

smugglers-run.purpose: a run for goods that never paid the town's tolls

built: the landing
a ledge with iron rings set in the wall, where boats were tied
the tally room
a room with a long plank table and a rack for lamps
the bonded store
a store with racks on every wall, built for bales
natural: the boat cave
a cave with water in it, a rotten jetty along one side
the dry ledge
a ledge above the waterline, scraped flat for stacking
the lookout crevice
a crack in the rock with a view back down the way in

traces: Tally marks are cut in the wall in long rows of five, hundreds of them: {builders} counted cargo here.
A rusted lantern hangs with its shutter on one side only, the kind that shows a light to one direction and no other.
Somebody has scratched a crude map of the town's streets into the plaster, with the watch-houses crossed out.

garrison.who: soldiers of a lord nobody remembers
garrison.purpose: a strongpoint under the ground, to hold the place in a siege

built: the gatehouse
two arrow-slits looking down the stair, and a bar-socket either side of the door
the guardroom
benches and a weapon rack, long empty
the armoury
pegs for spears in rows, and a whetstone worn into a saddle

traces: A duty roster is painted on the wall: names of {builders}, a watch each, and the last watch never filled in.
Spent arrowheads lie thick against one wall, all pointing the same way, inwards.
Soldiers' scratchings by the door: a game board, a name, a count of days that stops at forty-one.

mine-works.purpose: a working, dug after a seam that ran deeper than anyone expected

dug: the bottom of a shaft, where the winding cage came down
a level dug below the old one, its props still sound
a steep chute the ore came down, polished by it
natural: the miners' entry
a natural cave the miners widened, pick-marks on the walls
the sorting floor
a flat floor of rock, heaps of spoil along its edges
the cut seam
a cave where a seam was followed into the rock and given up

traces: Tally boards hang by the shaft with pegs still in them: so many loads a shift, the work of {builders}.
The pick-marks change halfway along: the same seam, cut later by different hands and different tools.
A lamp-niche holds a little clay figure, put there for luck by somebody who dug here.

wizards-retreat.who: a mage who wanted no neighbours
wizards-retreat.purpose: a retreat for work the town would not have stood for

built: the warded stair
a stair whose every step is cut with a sign, the signs gone dull
the library
shelves to the ceiling, most of the books gone to pulp
the laboratory
a long bench burnt black in rings, and glass ground underfoot

traces: Notes in a cramped hand are pinned to the shelves, every one of them about the same experiment.
Chalk circles are drawn and redrawn on the floor, each one a little larger than the last.
A mirror hangs face to the wall, and somebody has nailed it there.

old-drains.purpose: the first drains, laid before the town above them was half its size

built: the outfall gate
a gate of iron bars across the old channel, rusted open
the settling tank
a deep square tank, the silt in it gone hard as clay
the sluice room
a room of wheels and rotten gates that once let the water through

traces: Every brick is stamped with the same mark, the mark of {builders}, and the newer drains above have no mark at all.
A tide line runs along the walls well above head height, from a flood nobody up top remembers.
A builders' plaque is set in the wall, its words worn away, a date that is only the shape of numbers.

treasury.who: a family that grew rich and frightened
treasury.purpose: a strong-room, dug to keep what the house above was worth

built: the strong-room stair
a narrow stair with a door at the top and another at the bottom
the steward's room
a writing desk and racks of tally sticks, split and mouldy
the wine vaults
barrel racks, and barrels stove in long ago

traces: The steward's ledgers are bound in leather stamped with the sign of {builders}, page after page of what came in.
Every lock in the place has been changed at least once: new iron over the marks of old.
A bell on a wire runs along the ceiling from the stair to the inner door, its clapper tied with a rag.

prison.who: the law of an older day
prison.purpose: a prison below the ground, for those who were not to be seen again

built: the turnkey's room
a stool, a rack for keys, a slot in the door to look through
the cells
a row of cells, their doors hanging, chains still in the walls
the oubliette
a round room with a grate in the floor over a shaft

traces: Prisoners' marks cover the cell walls: names, days, and one long prayer cut letter by letter beside the seal of {builders} on the door.
The chains are short, and set low, so whoever wore them could never stand.
A sentence is painted over the door, the charges blacked out and the name left plain.

cavern.who: nobody: the water, over a long age
cavern.purpose: nothing; the water made it, and others found it afterwards

natural: the dripping gallery
water running down the walls into a hundred small pools
the flooded grotto
standing water, knee deep and very cold
the narrow cleft
a crack in the rock just wide enough to pass sideways

traces: The rock is carved by water into ribs and folds, older than any town; nothing made by hands stands here.
Old soot on the roof marks where somebody once kept a fire, a long time before anyone now.
Hand-prints in red ochre run along the wall at shoulder height, small ones and large ones together.

monastery.purpose: cells for an order that went below the ground to be away from the world

built: the gate cell
a cell by the door, with a bench for whoever kept the gate
the refectory
a long table cut from the rock itself, and stone bowls on it
the scriptorium
desks along the walls, ink pots dried to a crust
natural: the gate cave
a cave mouth with a wall and a narrow door built across it
the cells
small caves along a passage, each with a sleeping ledge
the cistern cave
a cave with a cistern cut in its floor, fed by a drip from above

traces: The rule of the order is cut into the wall by the door, line under line, in the hand of {builders}.
Each sleeping ledge has a name above it, and the last few names are in a different, hurried hand.
The bowls on the table are set for a meal, and the meal was never eaten.

ages.said: before the town above it had walls
so long ago that nobody living can say

_ages: With the world's chronology exported, an age is also 'in the days of <event>', the event's own name, drawn from the oldest half of the world's dated events.

ruin.said: a flood that filled it to the roof
ruin.trace: Silt lies a hand deep on every floor and a tide line runs along the walls high up: the water came all the way in, once.

ruin.said: a fire that ran through it
ruin.trace: The beams are charcoal, the plaster scorched black up one side of every room: the fire came from the way in.

ruin.said: a sickness that took the ones who kept it
ruin.trace: A heap of bedding was burned in the middle of the floor, and a sign is daubed on the door in something that was once lime.

ruin.said: a fall of the roof that cut it off
ruin.trace: Half of one wall is fallen rock, and old tools lie under it where somebody was digging through and stopped.

ruin.said: the war that took the land above it
ruin.trace: Spearheads and a split shield lie by the door: the place was held, and then it was not.

ruin.said: its own makers, who walled it up and left
ruin.trace: The doorway was walled up from this side with mortar and stones; the wall has been broken through since, from the other side.

ruin.said: a quarrel among the ones who kept it
ruin.trace: Two sets of marks are cut into the same wall, each one scratched out by the other.

ruin.said: the money running out, and the work stopped half done
ruin.trace: Tools are laid down mid-task along the far wall, a half-finished arch above them, as if the workers went up for wages and never came down.

users.trace: {users} slept here after: a fire-pit, bones of meals, and a knife-scored tally of shares.

users.who: the dead of a hard year
users.trace: Later bodies were laid here in haste, wrapped in sacking, by people who did not stop to cut names: {users}.
Over the old paint someone has drawn their own signs in soot, and candles have burned down to the floor in a ring where {users} gathered.
Rags and straw are piled in the corners, where beggars slept out the cold years after.

users.who: the town's watch, as a lockup
users.trace: A newer door was hung here with a bar on the outside, from the years the town's watch used the place as a lockup.
A rope, a broken lantern and a scratched warning lie where treasure-seekers turned back, or did not.
Families hid here once: little shoes, a cooking pot, a child's scratched drawing of the sky, left by {users}.

unlooted.said: the way in was lost, and nobody has found it since
it is said to be cursed, and nobody in {town} will go down
the few who went down did not come back up
{town} forbids it, and has for longer than anyone remembers
what lives there now keeps it

attitudes.said: Folk in {town} will not talk of {where} after dark
The children of {town} dare each other to go down into {where}, and none of them ever has
Only the old in {town} remember there was ever anything deeper than {where}
Every drinker in {town} has a story about treasure deep in {where}, and no two stories agree
In {town} they still leave a light for somebody who went down into {where} and never came back
In {town} they blame whatever is down in {where} for every bad season
